Thursday, November 12, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Thursday, Nov 12, 2026

Zelensky says Starshield speed limits are back on Ukraine's front line, hampering drone interception; Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow and are heading to Dublin to brief Zelensky, saying the next round may include the Europeans; some 50 European leaders and NATO's Rutte met at the European Political Community summit in Dublin.

← NewerFri, Nov 13, 2026All briefingsOlder →Wed, Nov 11, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: Ukraine says SpaceX's Starshield is again being speed-limited across the front line, which makes it harder to intercept jet-powered drones. U.S. envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin after the Abu Dhabi talks and said the next trilateral round may include the Europeans. Meanwhile, about 50 leaders gathered in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, where Ukraine and Russian hybrid threats dominated the agenda.

NATO

  • Speaking in Oslo aboard HMS Prince of Wales, Rutte said European allies and Canada are expected to spend more than $250 billion extra on core defence across 2025–26. He also welcomed the UK's pledge to reach 3% of GDP by 2030 as "a credible path" to 3.5%. (NATO)
  • Rutte said the Abu Dhabi talks brought positive developments, but that "it all depends on the Russians, whether they are willing to play ball," and that Ukraine must be kept as strong as possible. (The Guardian)
  • NATO Deputy SACEUR John Stringer said only Ukraine can decide on its territory and saw almost no sign that Putin is dropping his maximalist demands. SACEUR Grynkewich is advising U.S. negotiators in his EUCOM role. (RBC-Ukraine)
  • In a follow-up on the Baltic drone night, Lithuania's defence chief said two shoot-down attempts failed. He added that the drones may have been diverted by electronic warfare during Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Ust-Luga area, but their origin is unconfirmed. (The Globe and Mail / Reuters)

European Union

  • About 50 leaders, including Rutte and Canada's Carney, met at the ninth European Political Community summit in Dublin. Zelensky briefed the summit on the Abu Dhabi talks, an informal EU leaders' meeting follows on Nov. 13, and splits over Ukraine's €70B funding need for next year and the next long-term EU budget hang over both meetings. (RTÉ)
  • Defence and Space Commissioner Kubilius is in Rome and Turin on Nov. 12–13 for his "Launch Tour" on European access to space. He is meeting ministers Urso and Crosetto and visiting Avio (Vega) and Thales Alenia Space. (Agenzia Nova)
  • At its second board meeting, the Commission's EU–Ukraine Drone Alliance adopted its governance and elected Quantum Systems (EU) and UFORCE (Ukraine) as co-chairs. Its priorities are scaling up drone and counter-drone production and joint testing. (European Commission)

United States

  • The Space Force activated SPACEFOR-SOC at MacDill AFB as U.S. Special Operations Command's newest service component, the first since 2006. It will provide teams of "SOF Guardians" to theater special-operations commands. (U.S. Space Command / MacDill AFB)
  • Space Systems Command extended its RFI on Epoch 3 and 4 medium-Earth-orbit missile-warning/tracking satellites to Dec. 1 and plans to use firm-fixed-price OTAs. Meanwhile, the first Epoch 1 launch has slipped to 2027. (Defence Blog)
  • SpaceX launched the classified USSF-627 mission on Falcon 9 from Vandenberg at 8:36 p.m. PT on Nov. 11, its second Space Force mission in six days. Experts suspect more Starshield satellites for the Space Force's space-based sensing and targeting work. (Space.com)
  • Congress's lame-duck session now has to deal with the stalled FY27 defense bills and the NDAA. Analysts consider the $1.5 trillion request dead and a $350B reconciliation bill unlikely, and the current CR runs out Dec. 11. (Air & Space Forces Magazine)
  • A new Congressional Research Service insight lays out strategic-stability questions Congress may weigh when funding or overseeing Golden Dome. (USNI News)
  • GAO found the Pentagon still can't reliably track F-35 spare parts. About 17,000 parts worth up to $2.5B are missing from its logistics system, out of a roughly $31B joint spares pool. (Defense News)
  • Anduril unveiled three satellite payloads it has tested in orbit, including an infrared sensor that tracks spacecraft in Earth's shadow. (SpaceNews)
  • York Space Systems is buying Australian military robot maker Outlook Industries to set up an unmanned ground-systems business. (SpaceNews)
  • The Senate Commerce Committee will vote Nov. 18 on Joshua Shoemaker as NASA CFO and Robert Steinau as inspector general. NASA has lacked a confirmed CFO since January 2025. (SpaceNews)
  • Space Systems Command and UT Austin opened BMC3I TAP Lab Texas for early-stage space-domain-awareness software, funded by a $9.27M Texas Space Commission grant. (ExecutiveGov)

European space

  • ESA's Euclid published DR1-Foundation, its first major data release. It covers more than 900 million galaxies and about 1.7 million GB of data over 1,900 deg², and the full DR1 is due in mid-2027. (ESA)
  • ESA's Hera has reached the Didymos–Dimorphos pair and begun early characterisation from 25–30 km away. It moves in to about 20 km next month, and detailed images are due Nov. 25. (ESA)
  • Coming up: Ariane 6's 10th flight (VA271/LE-04) is set to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites no earlier than Nov. 23. That would bring the number Arianespace has deployed for Amazon to 136. (Arianespace)

Global space & defense

  • Zelensky said Starshield is again under "systematic" speed limits above 161 km/h across the front line, letting some Russian jet drones get through. A European official said the limits appeared as the Abu Dhabi talks began, and Kyiv wants to renew its Starshield contract, which ends in mid-2027. (Politico Europe; CNBC)
  • Witkoff and Kushner met Putin at the Kremlin. Witkoff said they are "resetting the trilateral talks" and hope to announce a next round that includes the Europeans, and the envoys then fly to Dublin to brief Zelensky. (Kremlin)
  • Putin suggested a "humanitarian mission" in contested Kostiantynivka. Kyiv warned that the last one, in Oleshky, was used to rotate Russian troops. (Kyiv Independent)
  • Xi said Taiwan's "reunification" must and will happen peacefully, a week before he meets Trump at APEC in Shenzhen. On the same day, Taiwan reported 29 Chinese aircraft on a "joint combat readiness patrol." (NBC News / Reuters; TaiwanPlus)
  • China is recruiting international partners for a 34-satellite cislunar constellation in nine-day elliptical orbits reaching lunar distance, with launch targeted for 2030. (SpaceNews)
